_comment: Voice-over script for the Scheduling composition. `budget` is the scene's designed length in seconds; build-narration.mjs stretches a scene if its line needs longer, so overruns are safe. Each line is generated as its own clip, so no splitting is involved.

lines.text: 744 recurring inspections. None of them land on a weekend.
Add N days, repeat. But the work week runs Sunday to Thursday, so two inspections in seven land on a weekend.
So push it to Sunday. Now Sunday carries 381 tasks. The problem moved. It did not go away.
Instead, every activity gets a permanent weekday, from a hash of its id. Deterministic, so 381 activities spread themselves evenly across the five working days.
Cadences of a week or more snap to that weekday, up to three days either way. The nearest one, never the next one.
Here is the trap. Measure the next cycle from the corrected date, and every correction carries forward. Four cycles in, a monthly inspection is six days late.
The result: 744 tasks, between 131 and 165 on every working day, and zero on a weekend.
It runs as a Postgres function, so the rules live next to the data, not in a job server that can quietly stop.
A scheduler is not a loop over dates. It is a set of decisions about the week people actually work.
